utterances.text: I don't think I understood it properly, maybe. But as an accompanying consequence of the failure to respond to the call-up was dismissal from jobs, the taking away of apartments, and similar acts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that was not subject to any legal remedy you could file against this judgement? I mean, the judgement was apart from the other consequences; is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Absolutely apart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I hope, Ms. Karagiannakis, that that's -- that we now all understood your question and that we, of course, understand the answer of the witness. Yes. Then, Mr. Odobasic, this concludes your testimony in this court. We'd like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague, to have answered all the questions by the parties and by the Bench. As you know, we have not only the information contained in your testimony of today, but it's also your statement is in evidence, so it's not limited specifically to what you said today. I just want you to know that. I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to thank you for those kind words, and I should like to hope that in your mission for the truth, you persevere and that you bring justice to bear for one and all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Odobasic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any further procedural issues? I noticed that it's already close to 2.00, and I again have to apologise to the interpreters. But as you are aware, the Chamber would really try to avoid a witness to stay over the weekend just for ten or fifteen remaining minutes. But we are aware that it's only with your assistance and with your flexibility, that we can do it. This is a warning to the parties not to take much more time on exhibits. I would say for this witness we could do them, but not for Mr. Radic, who -- these exhibits are still pending. Ms. Karagiannakis, you would like to tender the exhibits, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KARAGIANNAKIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher -- Mr. Registrar, could you please call them briefly so that we know what exhibits we are talking about and that we hear any objections, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that we're talking about Exhibit P366.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the -- yes. We are talking about -- no. There might be some misunderstanding. I'd like you to read on from 363, because they have got a number but they are not admitted in evidence. So what I see we have, P363, which is a document with, as it says, a -- stemming from the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of the Interior. It's dated 23rd of September, 1991. We have P364, which is a report from the Security Services Centre Banja Luka, dated the 20th of September, 1991. We have a clip from the -- I think it was the -- yes, it's Glas newspaper, of the 21st -- it's the newspaper of the 21st of April, 1992, with an article called "notice for a quarter," dating the 20th of April. And then we have 366, which is a bundle of documents concerning court proceedings against Mr. Odobasic in relation to his failure to respond to a mobilisation call.

utterances.speaker: MS. KARAGIANNAKIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is the matter of the statement -- which is marked P362 and P362.1. I understand my friend had an objection to the last paragraph. I agree to it being struck in light of the witness as evidence here today. So that should also be proffered -- we also offer that as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that solve the problem, then?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed it does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber would like to receive, at least for the Registry, one copy where the last paragraph is taken out. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: To any of the exhibits that have been proffered by the Prosecution? No, Your Honour. I indicated prior to the testimony at the beginning that I objected to 62. That matter -- paragraph 62. That's been settled, and I think perhaps the interpreters might like to go home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately we have to take a decision. The P Exhibits 362 up to and including 366 are admitted in evidence. Then we'll deal with whatever procedural issues next week and not at this moment. We'll adjourn until next Monday, but I think it's in the morning hours. The parties are -- 9.00. It's in the morning, it's at 9.00. Courtroom II? Well, the parties should verify whether the indication of the courtroom is correct or not. I wish you all a good weekend. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of November 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 24
